newsitem.title: UK: George Wimpey gains on budget relief.
newsitem.headline: George Wimpey gains on budget relief.

text.p: Shares in construction group George Wimpey Plc led other house builders higher on Thursday as investors breathed a sigh of relief that the Chancellor had not taken stronger measures to curb rising house prices, dealers said.
George Wimpey shares gained 6p to 143-1/2p by 0910 GMT.

In an attempt to cap recent house price rises, the Chancellor in Wednesday's budget raised stamp duty on property sales of over 250,000 stg by 0.5 percent to 1.5 percent and by one percent to two percent for house sales of more than 500,000 stg.
But dealers said the stamp duty increases would only affect a small proportion of house purchases, mainly in south-east England, leaving the rest of the housing market largely unaffected.

Dealers said shares in the house builders were also buoyed after mortgage tax relief was not abolished, as originally feared by investors. Instead the rate is to be reduced from 15 percent to 10 percent.
Elsewhere in the sector, Barratt Developments Plc rose 6p to 259p, Bellway Plc gained 11p to 346-1/2p and Berkeley Group Plc advanced 13-1/2p to 716p.
